original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-quasi-affine}
Let $A$ be a ring and let $U \subset \Spec(A)$ be a quasi-compact
open subscheme. For $\mathcal{F}$ quasi-coherent on $U$ the canonical map
$$
\widetilde{H^0(U, \mathcal{F})}|_U \to \mathcal{F}
$$
is an isomorphism.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 2412 takes U a QUASI-COMPACT open in affine Spec(A) and quasi-coherent F on U, and asserts the canonical sheafification of its H0 sections restricts isomorphically to F. No separatedness or flatness assumption is added.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-invert-f-affine}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $f \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$.
Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and assume that
$X_f$ is affine. Then the canonical morphism
$$
j : X \longrightarrow \Spec(\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X))
$$
from Schemes, Lemma \ref{schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine}
induces an isomorphism of $X_f = j^{-1}(D(f))$ onto the standard affine
open $D(f) \subset \Spec(\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X))$.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 2432 requires qcqs X and affine principal-open X_f, concluding its canonical affinization morphism identifies X_f with the standard affine D(f) of Spec global sections. Stage A keeps the qcqs and X_f affine assumptions and inverse-image assertion.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-affine}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Then $X$ is quasi-affine if and only if
the canonical morphism
$$
X \longrightarrow \Spec(\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X))
$$
from Schemes, Lemma \ref{schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine} is
a quasi-compact open immersion.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 2451 characterizes quasi-affine X by its canonical global-section map being a QUASI-COMPACT open immersion, not an arbitrary open immersion. The draft keeps the precise condition.

stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 2493 gives the stated cartesian square for an open immersion U→V of quasi-affine schemes and the induced affinization maps; the prepared square reproduces all schemes and arrows, without changing cartesianness.
statement:
Let $U \to V$ be an open immersion of quasi-affine schemes. Then
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[d] \ar[rr]_-j & & \Spec(\Gamma(U, \mathcal{O}_U)) \ar[d] \\
U \ar[r] & V \ar[r]^-{j'} & \Spec(\Gamma(V, \mathcal{O}_V))
}
$$
is cartesian.
hypotheses: Let $U \to V$ be an open immersion of quasi-affine schemes.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-affine-presentation}
Let $X$ be a quasi-affine scheme. There exists an integer $n \geq 0$,
an affine scheme $T$, and a morphism $T \to X$ such that for every
morphism $X' \to X$ with $X'$ affine the fibre product $X' \times_X T$
is isomorphic to $\mathbf{A}^n_{X'}$ over $X'$.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 2521 asserts a quasi-affine X has some affine T→X and fixed integer n≥0 such that for EVERY affine X'→X the base change is isomorphic to affine n-space over X'. The existential T,n precede the universal X' quantifier in the draft.
